c8-01-cold.text: Hello? Is this thing on? Anybody? Oh! Hey! I'm Glitchy. What's your name?

c8-02-name.text: Aw, look at you leanin’ in. That mic’s been busted since September. Light works wicked good, though.

c8-03-clippy.text: Call me Clippy, and you'll find out how hard it is to click Skip Tutorial with a trackpad in your mouth. Bored? Skip a section. I won't take it personally. Welcome to the Chop Shop.

c8-04-left.text: Three example packs to start with. Generate as often as you like: a new song every time. Got samples of your own? Add your pack. Or Find samples: listen through any folder, keep the good ones. Need more? Resources: where to get them, free and paid. Crate digging, minus the back pain.

c8-05-pack.text: Start from scratch, or pick a pack. Main Stage: EDM. Subtle as a foam cannon.

c8-06-style.text: Then, how hard to chop. One shots plays the pack's song as it was made. Chop cuts it up into new parts. Experimental lets chance in. Hit Generate, and I sketch a starting point. Not your song: an idea of how the sounds could fit. You do the rest. I just hold the flashlight.

c8-07-pads.text: Here's a sketch I made earlier. Every pad, every chop: yours to wreck. Down here, the pads. Every row's a track, every lit pad a hit. Click to add one, click again to lose it. Commitment issues? Command Z.

c8-08-drag.text: Drag a box over the pads, and change them all at once. Glitch them. Mass edits. Like taxes, but fun.

c8-09-takes.text: Pick a track, and it takes the stage. Roll the dice: your sample, ripped apart and welded into a new riff.

c8-10-evidence.text: Every roll's a take. They're all kept. Like evidence. Zero's the original.

c8-11-step.text: Flip to Step, and it's one hit. Its dice rolls a riff inside that one chop.

c8-12-chance.text: Its dials are its own: pitch, level, even its odds. Sixty percent. Like my warranty.

c8-13-mods.text: Track Mods: everything you can bolt onto a track. Warranty void if bolted.

c8-14-auto.text: Automation draws a move across the bar: a swell, a fade, a filter opening. Very dramatic. Very French.

c8-15-melody.text: Melody turns a vocal into a hook, in key. Every roll's a new take. Glitch Chop: pitched up, stuttered, still in tune. And you pick how many sections it plays in.

c8-15b-comets.text: Fold it, and down here you watch it sing. Comets! Somebody gave the vocal a planetarium budget.

c8-16-song.text: Up top, the whole song, track by track. A bird's-eye view. If the bird had a DAW.

c8-17-fork.text: That's the basics: a sketch, and the tools to wreck it. Want the deep cuts? That's where the power is. Or go make something loud. I won't cry. No tear ducts.

c8-18-length.text: The hi-hats: sixteen steps. Slide them to twelve, and they drift against the bar. Twelve steps. The hi-hats are in recovery.

c8-19-even.text: Click the handle: Even hits spreads them out, the math way. Speed: half time to double time.

c8-20-poly.text: Mono cuts a hit off at the next one. Poly lets it ring. Set it on the track, and every hit follows.

c8-21-bus.text: The FX Bus: one shared chain, made for your genre when you Generate. Slide how much of each track goes in. A tip jar. For reverb.

c8-22-synth.text: Synthesis: a wavetable, built from your own sample. Give it a spin. Every hit, a little different. It's not a bug. It's a personality.

c8-23-effects.text: Effects: real LUNA plugins on the track, their dials right here. Plugins. Plural. Look at you.

c8-24-trim.text: Double-click a hit to trim it: drag either end, even past its chop. Snip snip.

c8-25-split.text: Split: one step, three quick hits. Hi-hat rolls, no carpal tunnel. Flam: a ghost hit just ahead.

c8-26-looks.text: Make it yours: the keys, and what each track's label shows. Neon? Or LUNA's own.

c8-27-sounds.text: No sound for the part in your head? Describe it, and your AI key makes it. Your key, your bill. I just work here.

c8-28-outro.text: That's the tour. Now go make it yours. Great work, uh... you. Hit it.

c8-29-bye.text: Been practicing. And if anybody asks... you never saw me.

c8-16b-build.text: Build turns your loop into a song: a drop, a break, a swell. Hear it climb? And right before the chorus, everything bends up. Add it, and the song grows. Like mold, but good.

c8-13b-arp.text: First, the Arp: every hit becomes an arpeggio of the chord underneath. Two octaves. Fancy word for showing off.

c8-03b-byosp.text: Quick question. B.Y.O.S.? Bring your own samples. Or test drive mine. Fair warning: they're basic. Bargain-bin crunchy.

own-01-sorted.text: Sorted. Let's build something out of it.

own-02-kick.text: Give me a kick. Click one to hear it.

own-03-snare.text: Now a snare. Or a clap. I don't judge.

own-06-music.text: Now the music. Chords, keys, a loop.

own-07-vocal.text: A vocal? Totally optional. Like pants on a video call.

own-09-keep.text: All yours. Keep it, or let me show you round the shop.

wait-01.text: Ooh, that's a big one. Loading up the truck with your samples.

wait-02.text: That's a lot of inventory. We're gonna have to sort all this out. Kicks over here, snares over there.

wait-03.text: This might take a minute. Keep a lookout for me.

wait-04.text: Still loading. Nice sounds in here, by the way.

wait-done.text: Okay! Truck's loaded. Let's build something out of it.
